messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall-elaine (sev2) - Elevated p99 tail latency for short/interactive requests in us-east-1. Observed KV cache "blowup" (rapid growth of active entries) + continuous batching pack sizes increasing -> starvation of short requests. Autogenerated alert group: kv.cache.eviction.rate high, batch.scheduler.p99_lat > 1s. Please acknowledge and triage.

oncall-elaine: ack I'm on it, jumping into logs and metrics now. tagging eng-kv and ml-runtime.

sre-anna: oncall - quick note: dashboards show spike started ~00:58 UTC, correlates with a rollout of prefetch pump on small-inference pool (rolling out config kv_prefetch: aggressive) at 00:56. Short requests p99 went from ~180ms -> 1.4s.

eng-kv: confirming rollout. We flipped kv_prefetch=true on pool "inference-small" earlier as a perf experiment to improve long-run throughput; looks like it increased active KV usage and pack sizes for continuous batching.

ml-runtime: logs show pack sizes growing to 512-1024 for mixed requests. Short requests are being coalesced into huge packs; scheduler favors throughput and long requests keep monopolizing GPU windows.

oncall-elaine: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle prefetch, 2) cap pack size lower, 3) temporarily bias scheduler to prioritize short requests. Which can we do fastest?

ops-maria: I can revert the prefetch flag in the rollout (k8s patch) within 90s. Also can push a config to batch-scheduler to cap max_pack to 256.

platform-lead: recommend two-prong: revert prefetch immediately + push scheduler cap. Revert is lowest risk. Also prepare a hotfix to add short_request_priority gating.

eng-kv: preparing revert now. Patch: `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/kv-prefetcher PREFETCH_MODE=conservative` and rotate pods.

incidents-bot: runbook invoked: /runbook kv_cache_continuous_batching (link)

ops-maria: running revert...

ops-maria: done - rollout completed at 01:02:34 UTC. PREFETCH_MODE=conservative on inference-small. Pods restarted.

oncall-elaine: good. eng-kv, can you push scheduler cap in parallel?

eng-kv: applying runtime override to batch scheduler (hotpatch):
```yaml
# temp override
batch_scheduler:
  max_pack_size: 256
  short_request_priority: true
  prefetch_enabled: false  # emergency guard
```
Applying to us-east-1 scheduler via config service now.

eng-kv: hotpatch applied at 01:04:11 UTC. Confirming metrics..

ml-runtime: p99 for short requests dropped from ~1400ms -> ~240ms within two windows. p50 stable. Eviction rate trending down.

oncall-elaine: running full traffic check. Any customer-facing 5xx/429 spikes?

customer-success-jay: We're seeing some 429s from a few mid-tier customers between 00:58-01:03 UTC (peak). No persistent errors; we opened tickets and proactively messaged 3 accounts with elevated errors. No data loss reported.

eng-kv: note: we observed a backlog on pack allocation queue; pack allocator had an O(N) path that amplified under aggressive prefetch. Short requests were starving because large packs held cache pins. We'll follow up with a code patch to early-yield on short_request tag.

sre-anna: temporary mitigations confirm: revert prefetch + scheduler cap reduced impact. Next steps: codefix for allocator fairness, add metric for average pack_hold_time, refine alert thresholds for pack size and eviction rate.

platform-lead: create an action item list and assign owners. Also set alert to page at lower threshold so we catch earlier.

oncall-elaine: documenting timeline for handoff: root cause tied to prefetch rollout + scheduler fairness degeneracy. Hotfix applied, customer impact limited and notified. I'll hand off to leo-nightoncall for the overnight watch at 01:33 UTC.

leo-nightoncall: ack - taking over at 01:33 UTC. Summary understood. Points for night: 1) keep telemetry on pack_size/p99 for short reqs; 2) if p99 creeps > 600ms re-enable strict short_request_priority and scale pool; 3) if eviction rate > 70% escalate to eng-kv.

sre-anna: adding follow-ups: (a) eng-kv to open PR for allocator fairness with bench, target fix in next 48h, (b) telemetry team to add pack_hold_time and split alerts for mixed workload, (c) product to document behavior for dedicated customers.

eng-kv: opened GH PR #4890 with reproducer and proposed fix: early_yield_on_short_requests. Performance bench included.

customer-success-jay: sent 1:1 updates to affected customers (guidance + root cause + ETA for permanent fix). Customers asked for postmortem once complete.

oncall-elaine: creating incident summary for postmortem. Key metrics to include: p99 short req latency pre/post, eviction rate, pack size distribution, affected customer list, timeline of actions.

ops-maria: left note: rollback was safe; no config drift expected. Saved hotspot nodes logs at s3://redwood-incidents/1719129999/ for eng review.

incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigation applied, monitoring. No active customer-impacting errors reported past 01:10 UTC.

leo-nightoncall: quick check at 01:45 UTC: p99 at 260ms, eviction rate 18%, pack median 48. Looks stable. I'll monitor and escalate if anything changes.

oncall-elaine: handing off full details in #incidents-docs. Leaving a short note for postmortem owners. Great job team. :thumbsup:

sre-anna: marking action items in tracker and assigning eng-kv, telemetry. Will schedule postmortem sync tomorrow.

eng-kv: follow-up note: rollout experiment parameters need stricter canary (traffic-shadow 5% for 10m) before global flip. We'll update release checklist.

customer-success-jay: customers acknowledged update, appreciate proactive contact. No escalations.

incidents-bot: This thread will remain open until postmortem is filed. Closing hands off to night oncall leo-nightoncall.

leo-nightoncall: closing loop here at 02:00 UTC - monitoring continues, will reopen if regressions observed.
